clue.text: A hunch new job could be the making of author

indicators.note: the letters of the words before could be remade into something new, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A writer's lucky hunch about a fresh job turns out to launch a literary career.
explanation.walkthrough: 'could be the making of' signals the anagram of A HUNCH, N and JOB. JOHN BUCHAN was a Scottish novelist, author of The Thirty-Nine Steps.
explanation.definitionFit: The Scottish novelist who wrote The Thirty-Nine Steps is an example of an author.

clue.text: One ultimately gets stick over possible future sacking

indicators.note: in a down clue the first piece sits over the next

parts.note: to jut is to stick out

indicators.note: taking just the final letter of One

explanation.surface: Someone ends up under the stick, with a likely firing ahead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sacking' suggests dismissal but means coarse cloth.
explanation.definitionFit: This coarse plant fibre is woven into hessian bags, so it is material that may become sacking.

clue.text: Bullies clipping animal's tail: shocking way to treat cuts

indicators.note: the treatment cuts into the clipped animal
clipping the tail means the last letter of the animal is cut off

parts.note: a horse is an animal
ECT is electroconvulsive therapy, treatment by electric shock

explanation.surface: Bullies dock an animal's tail, a shocking way to deal with wounds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'clipping animal's tail' takes the E from HORSE; ECT goes into HORS.
explanation.definitionFit: To browbeat or bully someone is to hector them, so the verbs are synonyms.

clue.text: Astounding soldiers should get into the habit of washing!

indicators.note: the soldiers get into the phrase for washing habits

parts.note: bath-taking is the habit of washing in a bath

explanation.surface: An exclamation that soldiers really ought to start washing regularly.
explanation.walkthrough: RE stands for the Royal Engineers, a British Army corps; 'the habit of washing' is taken as one hyphenated phrase, bath-taking.
explanation.definitionFit: Something so astonishing it makes you gasp is described as stunning in this way.

clue.text: Dishes of copper turned up small and all the same

parts.note: Cu is the chemical symbol for copper

indicators.note: in a down clue the word is turned upwards, i.e. read backwards

parts.note: yet means all the same, nevertheless

explanation.walkthrough: 'turned up' reverses YET to TEY. 'Dishes' is slang for attractive people.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang for attractive people, crossword-friendly sense: a dish is a good-looking person.

clue.text: Extra bit from novel I quietly expand

parts.note: p is piano, quietly in music

explanation.walkthrough: 'novel' looks like a book but signals the anagram of I, P and EXPAND.
explanation.definitionFit: Supplementary matter at the end of a book is an addition, and the body organ is also a small extra part.

clue.text: Mine is definitely not to be hit!

definitions.meaning: an explosive device buried or laid to blow up
a show or film that flops badly, the opposite of a success

explanation.surface: A warning that this explosive must on no account be struck.
explanation.walkthrough: The second sense is the theatre and film usage: a production that fails completely, so it is anything but a hit.
explanation.definitionFit: A mine is a kind of explosive device, and a total commercial flop is the slang opposite of a hit.

clue.text: Having this one's evidently not restricted view

parts.note: O as zero, nothing, i.e. not any

explanation.surface: Someone with this outlook is plainly unconstrained.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the answer as 0 PINION: with zero binding, one is evidently not restricted.
explanation.definitionFit: A view held on a matter is a belief or judgement, a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: Idea showers — cold and hot — should be taken in Berlin daily

indicators.note: the weather pieces are taken inside the newspaper's name

rain falls in showers

clue.text: Sort of welcome volunteers exercising on watch perhaps

explanation.walkthrough: TA, the Territorial Army, is Britain's part-time volunteer reserve force.
explanation.definitionFit: A parade showered with paper streamers is a celebratory kind of reception, so the term describes a sort of welcome.

clue.text: Say how spy comes to that city

parts.note: the letter of the word spy that differs from the word say

the letter of the word say that stands where spy has its P

explanation.surface: A traveller explaining how an undercover agent arrives at a particular city.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue asks how 'spy' becomes 'Say': its P is (comes to) an A. Split the city's name after its first letter and it states that swap.
explanation.definitionFit: The Tuscan town famous for its leaning tower is the place meant by the pointing phrase.

clue.text: Warned of being behind, European's previously needed to pay

had marks the past perfect, what happened previously
owed means needed to pay

explanation.surface: A warning about falling into arrears, as a European has had to pay up.
explanation.definitionFit: To hint at something in advance is to give warning of it, a close synonym.

clue.text: Travelling beauty has writer go home with proposal

parts.note: Edgar Allan Poe, the American writer
a go is an attempt, a try

a motion is a proposal put to a meeting

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes something moving gracefully, so beauty in movement fits a travelling beauty.

clue.text: Port originally kept to oneself getting drunk

taking only the first letter of kept

explanation.surface: Someone who kept to themselves gets drunk on port.

explanation.definitionFit: A Kent harbour town on the Channel coast is an example of a port.

clue.text: Handy for location shooting so no questions asked, we hear?

indicators.note: says the words before are taken as they sound when spoken

parts.note: to shoot on sight is to fire at once without asking questions

explanation.surface: A film crew's place that is convenient for filming on location.
explanation.walkthrough: 'location shooting' looks like a film term, but shooting belongs to the wordplay: shooting on sight, with no questions asked.
explanation.definitionFit: Something placed right at the location is conveniently near, which is how handy is meant.

clue.text: During short recess no German needing to be driven a long way home?

indicators.note: the German word goes during, that is within, the shortened recess

explanation.definitionFit: A long nail, such as a nine-inch one, has to be hammered a long way in, i.e. driven home.

clue.text: Attire to go on over white coat?

definitions.text: Attire to go on over white coat?

parts.words: Attire to go on over white coat?

clue.text: Operating canoe or a yacht, initially similar in weight

clue.text: Part of Mexico that's revolting — not quite what sun-seeker hopes for?

clue.text: Hotel's not heated but man providing room service may be in

a chap is a man

clue.text: Player's seemingly good answer isn't, surprisingly

clue.text: First statement from witness can't stand: case dismissed
